contexts.text: Oxen,etc., when sacrificed, = lower celestial things.
That the Lord put on also a conformable Natural, is signified by the son of an ox ().
When oxen and bullocks appear in the World of Spirits, they know that the Angels are discoursing about natural goods.

Abraham took the son of an ox tender and good = the Celestial Natural which the Rational received to itself, in order that it might conjoin itself with perception from the Divine. A bullock, or son of an ox, in the Word, = natural good.
The Celestial Natural is signified by the son of an ox.
The son of an ox = the Natural corresponding.
The sacrifice of an ox represented natural good.
Voluntary things, which are of good, are signified by oxen, etc.
To send the foot of the ox and the donkey () = natural things which will serve (for instruction). The ox = the Natural as to good.
The ox and the donkey = natural good and truth. Illustrated.

I had ox and donkey... () = acquisitions in their order there. An ox and donkey, etc. = exterior goods and truths which are of service... An ox = exterior natural good; and a donkey, exterior natural truth.

In their good-pleasure they hamstrung an ox () = that in evil of purpose they extinguished the good of the Church. ( = that from a depraved will they completely debilitated the external good which is of charity. AC 6357. AE 443:6.)
Flocks, and oxen () = goods internal and external.
Cows, or heifers, = the truths of the Natural; (for) oxen, and bullocks = the goods of the Natural...
An ox, and a bullock = the goods of the Natural (References.); here, the goods of the exterior Natural...
To plough = preparation by good for the reception of truths; for the oxen with which the ploughing was done = goods in the Natural. References.
Hence it was forbidden to plough with an ox and a donkey together ()... because to plough with an ox = good in the Natural. (Continued. See Donkey.)
An ox = the natural or external good of charity. References.
The oxen and cows (in Mercury) do not differ much from those in our Earth, but are smaller; and in a certain way approach a species of deer. SE 3262.

An ox = the good of the Natural... That they were not to plough with an ox and a donkey together = that they were not to be in both states together; namely, in good, and thence look to truth; and at the same time in truth, and thence look to good.
An ox (in the tenth commandment) = the affection of natural good; (which) is not to be coveted, that is, taken away from anyone, or injured.

When an ox shall gore a man or woman () = if the affection of evil in the Natural shall injure the truth or the good of faith... An ox = the affection of good in the Natural; hence, in the opposite sense, the affection of evil in the Natural. AC 9069.
If the ox is a goring one from yesterday the day before yesterday () = if there has long been the affection of evil.
The ox shall be stoned () = the penalty of destroyed truth.
If the ox gores a man-servant, or a maidservant () = if the affection of evil shall destroy truth or good in the Natural. AC 9079.

The ox shall be stoned () = the penalty of destroyed truth and good in the Natural... In the Natural, because it is an ox which shall be stoned, by which is signified the affection in the Natural which has committed destruction.
And an ox or a donkey has fallen (into the pit) () = (the falsity) which perverts the good or truth in the Natural. An ox = the affection of evil in the Natural; thus evil there.
An ox = good in the Natural.

When a man's ox has struck a companion's ox a blow () = two truths of which the affections are diverse, and that of the one has injured that of the other... An ox = the affection of good; and, in the opposite sense, the affection of evil, in the Natural; and a man = truth... The reason diverse affections are signified, is that it is oxen which injure one another; for the things which are diverse injure one another; but not those which are not diverse.
In the Spiritual World... when the affections of good in the Natural are presented to view in an animal form, they appear as gentle oxen; and the affections of evil, as fierce oxen.
The ox which died from the blow struck by the other ox = a good affection.
They shall sell the live ox () = that the affection of the one which injured that of the other shall be alienated.

The dead one also they shall divide () = also the injuring affection... By the dead ox is signified the affection of evil and falsity in the Natural; thus the injuring affection; for evil injures through falsity. Explained.
If it was known that the ox was a goring one from yesterday the day before yesterday () = that it was known before that such was the affection.
Repaying he shall repay ox for ox () = restitution to entirety... An ox = an affection in the Natural.
a. The dead one shall be his own () = for the injuring affection. The ox = the affection of evil.
When a man has stolen an ox, or a small cattle () = him who takes away from anyone his exterior or interior good... An ox = the affection of good in the Natural; thus exterior good. References.
Five oxen shall he repay for the ox () = a corresponding penalty to a great extent.
From an ox even to a donkey () = from exterior good or truth. An ox = the good of the Natural.
When a man has given to his companion a donkey or an ox... to keep () = exterior and interior truth and good...
So shalt thou do with thine ox, with thy flock () = that [this attribution to the Lord extends] to exterior and interior good.
When thou meetest thine enemy's ox, or his donkey, going astray () = good not genuine, and truth not genuine, with those outside the Church... An ox = the good of the external man.
An ox = the good of the external or natural man. References.
To send forth the foot of the ox and of the donkey = to be instructed in external goods and truths.
That thine ox may rest, and thine donkey () = the tranquillity of peace [enjoyed by] external goods and truths at the same time.
An ox () = good in the Natural; thus in the external form.
The purifications of the external man were represented by burnt-offerings and sacrifices of oxen, bullocks, and he-goats. AC 10042:8.
An ox = good.
The twelve oxen () = all the goods of the natural and sensuous man in the complex, because they were in the place of bases.
The oxen () = protection lest goods should enter; for oxen = goods in their power. References.
To plough with an ox () = to prepare by means of good. Explained.
Oxen and bullocks correspond to the affections of the natural mind.
An ox, etc. = natural affection.
In Egypt... there were images of calves, oxen, etc., because calves and oxen signified the affections and forces of the natural mind.
The perfect animals are oxen, etc.
Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's... ox, etc Explained.
An ox = natural good.
The first-born of an ox, honour is his () = the good of spiritual love.
To sacrifice an ox () = worship from those things which represented natural good.
Shall one plough with oxen? () = is there any perception of good?
The twelve oxen = all the goods and derivative truths upon which they are founded.
An ox, in the Word, = moral and natural good.
Oxen ploughing = the will of good.
a donkey and an ox () = the truth and good of the natural man.
Oxen, in the Word, = natural affections; and five yoke of oxen () = all these affections, or the cupidities which draw away from Heaven.
An ox () = the good of the natural man: that he shall repay five oxen for the ox = that he shall sufficiently amend the things he has perverted and extinguished.

That the face of an ox was seen on the left () = the good of truth in obscurity; for by an ox is signified the good of the natural man which is in obscurity with those who dwell in Heaven at the north.
To kill an ox and slay a small cattle () = to extinguish natural good and spiritual good.
The herds of the ox () = those things which are of the natural man in the whole complex.
Well-laden oxen () = natural goods and their affections.
The ark being brought upon a new cart to which oxen were attached () represented the doctrine of truth from the good of love... Oxen = the good of love in the natural man.

The lion shall eat straw like the ox () = that infernal falsity burning to destroy the truths of the Church will do no harm to the affection of good of the natural man; neither with a man in himself, nor with men among each other; and neither will it do harm to the Word. Explained.
The ox and donkey (in the tenth commandment) = the affection of natural good and truth.
In the World of Spirits are seen oxen, etc.
